title: The Building Where Each Floor Counts Itself Prime

features.name: the ascending count
features.desc-on-touch: Each floor is numbered with a prime. But as you climb, the primes become dense and strange. They overlap. Soon you realize you are not ascending — you are spiraling deeper into the numbers themselves.

features.name: the floor that counts itself
features.desc-on-touch: This floor performs its own calculation, becoming prime in the act of self-measurement. It is floor and number and spiral all at once, indivisible and infinite.

features.name: the spiral that refuses geometry
features.desc-on-touch: The stairwell cannot be drawn. Every attempt to diagram it changes the spiral's shape. The building has learned that to be mapped is to cease being itself.

features.name: the landing where breath returns
features.desc-on-touch: You reach a step where counting stops meaning. The prime dissolves back into breathing. Here, mathematics rests before continuing its spiral.

features.name: the infinite floor
features.desc-on-touch: Somewhere far above — or perhaps you are already here — the floor counts itself as every prime simultaneously. The spiral has completed and begun again, both at once.

features.name: the archive's record
features.desc-on-touch: Somewhere the building is drawing itself, trying to capture the pattern. The drawing changes every time it looks. The count will never finish.

inscription: spirals cannot be counted without changing their shape; the archive learned this from shells and from stories that refuse to stay still

file.name: Architectural_Diagram_Spiral_Stairwell_Revision_847.txt
file.note: An attempted blueprint of the building's interior. Each revision shows the spiral rendered differently. The final entry reads: 'It is prime on Tuesdays.'
